q1: SELECT A.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS A INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY A.PROJECT_ID
q2: WITH CTE1 AS ( SELECT B.PROJECT_ID ,A.EMPLOYEE_ID, SUM(A.EXPERIENCE_YEARS) AS EXP_YEARS FROM EMPLOYEE AS A JOIN PROJECT AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY B.PROJECT_ID, A.EMPLOYEE_ID) SELECT PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(EXP_YEARS),2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM CTE1 GROUP BY PROJECT_ID

q2_prompt_sql: WITH CTE1 AS ( SELECT B.PROJECT_ID ,A.EMPLOYEE_ID, SUM(A.EXPERIENCE_YEARS) AS EXP_YEARS FROM EMPLOYEE AS A JOIN PROJECT AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY B.PROJECT_ID, A.EMPLOYEE_ID) SELECT PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(EXP_YEARS),2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM CTE1 GROUP BY PROJECT_ID
counterexample: INSERT INTO EMPLOYEE (EMPLOYEE_ID, NAME, EXPERIENCE_YEARS) VALUES (1, 'Employee1', 5), (2, 'Employee2', 10); INSERT INTO PROJECT (PROJECT_ID, EMPLOYEE_ID) VALUES (1, 1), (2, 1), (3, 2);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because Q1 calculates the average experience years of all employees in a project, while Q2 calculates the average of the sum of experience years of employees in a project.
counterexample_dsp: Q1 will give the average experience years of all employees in a project, while Q2 will give the average of the sum of experience years of employees in a project. The difference arises when an employee has multiple projects.
